components.institution_label: Seven-Month Leave Period under New York State Domestic Relations Law
components.description: Unpaid child care leave of up to seven months from the date of delivery or adoption, mandatory on request of either parent; one parent at a time where both are State employees.
components.mechanism_note: Leave without pay that the documents attribute to Article 7 of the Domestic Relations Law (statute not saved); coded as a statutory leave with its length as the documents state it.
components.faculty_group_note: Employees of the Professional Services Negotiating Unit (UUP Appendix A-42, 'Family Leave—Professional Services Negotiating Unit'); HR page: 'All employees, regardless of sex'.
eligible_parent: any_parent
components.eligible_parent_wording: Employees, regardless of sex; either parent; following the date of delivery or adoption (HR page: also adoptive or foster parents)
components.entitlement_note: 'entitled'; 'mandatory upon request from either parent'; stated as a statutory entitlement.
components.duration_note: Up to seven months following delivery or adoption. Periods of disability or use of leave credits after delivery are included in, and do not extend, the seven months. A leave requested for less than seven months is extended on request to the maximum; beyond the seventh month the leave is at the discretion of the Chief Administrative Officer, except for continuing medical disability. Where the child must remain in hospital, the leave may start at release; hospital admission after the start suspends it; entitlement expires one year after the original start.
components.dual_employee_rule: If both parents are State employees, leave for child care is mandatory for one parent at a time; the parents may split it into two blocks, one continuous block each, not exceeding a combined seven months and not extending beyond seven months from the date of delivery; other shared or concurrent arrangements at campus discretion.
components.time_window: within seven months following the date of delivery or adoption
components.relief_note: Leave without pay; no relief stated (R9).

notes: Reference date 2018-02-24. 2018_00_link.txt is the HR Leaves of Absence page; 2018_01_fmla_description.txt is an FMLA brochure.

Governing documents for faculty leave are present: the State-UUP collective agreement (UB academic employees are in the Professional Services Negotiating Unit) and the SUNY Policies of the Board of Trustees (Art. XIII leaves; Art. XIX: where the agreement differs, it controls), with the UB Faculty/Staff Handbook IV. So missing is false.

No paid parental, maternity or childbirth leave exists in the saved documents for State-funded faculty: the childbirth disability period (generally about four weeks before to six weeks after delivery) is paid only from the employee's own accrued sick leave (and vacation for calendar-year employees; academic-year employees accrue no vacation). Additional sick leave at pay after accruals are exhausted is at the College President's discretion (c6).

The main parental entitlement is the seven-month unpaid child care leave (c1), stated in UUP Appendix A-42 V and on the HR page as a Domestic Relations Law Article 7 entitlement. Appendix A-42 says the appendices are 'not part of the collective bargaining agreement' and that its descriptions do not modify the original sources; the statute or State attendance rule it summarises is not saved. I coded it as a guaranteed statutory leave and flagged the source status.

Birth parent chain: own sick leave (disability from about four weeks before delivery, c5) runs inside the seven-month child care leave from delivery (c1) with FMLA alongside (c2); in the discretionary variant, additional paid sick leave (c6, up to six months including accruals) follows exhausted sick leave, then additional sick leave without pay (c7, up to one calendar year).
Non-birth parent chain: seven-month child care leave from delivery (c1) with FMLA alongside (c2); family sick leave from own balance (c11, 30 days a year) for care of the birth parent.
Calendar: the handbook (IV.I.II) refers to the fall and spring semesters for academic-year faculty; no term length is stated, so calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order.

Statutes and policies named but not saved: New York Domestic Relations Law Article 7; NY State Civil Service policies (breast milk expression, blood donation, cancer screening); NY Military Law s. 242; the Presidential Sick Leave Memo template; 'Appendix A-46 of the Policies of the Board of Trustees' (cited in A-42 VIII; not in the saved April 2017 Policies); Department of Civil Service Attendance and Leave Manual Appendix H (leave donation guidelines); US DOL FMLA fact sheet and 'Employee Rights and Responsibilities Under the FMLA'; State University Group Disability Insurance Program plan document.

HR page 'Personal Leave' ('If you are faculty represented by UUP, you may be eligible for personal leave') names no terms; the agreement provides no personal leave for academic-year faculty beyond the Title F leaves (c4); recorded here, not as a separate component.

UUP 23.12 and BOT XIII Title K: all leaves of absence terminate on expiration of a term appointment; tenure-track faculty hold term appointments, so leaves cannot extend beyond the current term (flagged on c1).

The 2011 tenure clock stop memo is a redacted sample, evidence of practice and not a policy text; it shows a one-year qualified appointment for the birth of a child. It supports c13 but sets no length.
The UB Faculty/Staff Handbook sections are marked current as of 1997 (leave) and 2000; they are consistent with the 2011-2016 agreement and the 2017 BOT Policies on the provisions used.

paid_caps.note: combined cap 6 calendar months on c5 and c6 (accrued plus additional paid sick leave)
